chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one in Ihram does not immerse himself in water, nor does the fasting person.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.يَرْتَمِسُ: to immerse oneself fully in water

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram or fasting immerse themselves completely in water?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific prohibition against full immersion (irtimas) for both the pilgrim in Ihram and the fasting individual, distinguishing it from general washing. Shia jurists interpret this as a precautionary measure to preserve the sanctity of the Ihram state and to avoid breaking the fast through excessive water intake or neglect of ritual purity norms. The ruling underscores the meticulous attention to physical states in Shia fiqh, linking bodily actions directly to spiritual validity.
